# Word Pattern.

@example m lines up with "tea" both times; n and o line up with "milk" and "coffee", two other words.
"mnmo"
"tea milk tea coffee"
=> true

@example The first two words are equal, but their letters, a and b, are not.
"abc"
"go go home"
=> false

@example Three words, but only two letters.
"zz"
"hi hi hi"
=> false

# One letter matches any single word, even one of 3000 letters.
"r"
""
=> true

# One letter and two words: too many words, though they are equal.
"a"
"go go"
=> false

# The first letters and words match, then a word is left over; and the
# other way round, a letter is left over.
"ab"
"cat dog cat"
=> false

"aba"
"cat dog"
=> false

# Words are compared whole: one is a prefix of the other, and two have
# the same length and first letter.
"ab"
"tap tape"
=> true

"aa"
"tip tap"
=> false

# Two words with the same letters in another order are still different
# words.
"pq"
"stop pots"
=> true

# Letters and words are never compared with each other: x lines up with
# "y" and y with "z", or x with "y" and y with "x".
"xy"
"y z"
=> true

"xy"
"y x"
=> true

# The first letter repeats but the first word doesn't, and the other way
# round.
"aba"
"x y z"
=> false

"abc"
"x y x"
=> false

# One letter throughout; only the last word differs.
"hhhhh"
"so so so so no"
=> false

# 26 different letters; the last word repeats the first.
"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"
"oak ash elm fir yew bay box fig gum ivy kauri larch maple neem olive palm quince rowan sumac teak ulmo vine walnut xylem yucca oak"
=> false
